nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: Red flowers on the Choir's white stone. This came down from the Manalith, and it isn't taking anything. I can feel that it isn't.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: The Herald says it all fell here: moss, blossom, beasts come back changed. The Wild live in it and nobody tithes them. Look at you. Out here nobody paid for you to breathe, and you're standing like you know it.

nodes.speaker: class-moorcaptain
nodes.line: Quota... You think the tithe stops with me? The Choir will send someone who doesn't keep count.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: Then they'll find the wagon gone and the waystone awake. Where does the colour go, Captain?

nodes.speaker: class-moorcaptain
nodes.line: Up the old road, to the Still, and past it. I never asked further. Nobody who asks comes back to the moor.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: Then we'll ask. Tell the holds their tithe is their own again.

nodes.speaker: class-moorcaptain
nodes.line: They won't believe it from me.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: They'll believe it from us.

nodes.speaker: class-hierarch
nodes.line: Thieves from the holds, in my own white wagon. Do you know how long my Choir has kept the Manalith asleep?

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: The Lullaby needs a thread of the tithe. You drank everything else.

nodes.speaker: class-hierarch
nodes.line: Twelve hundred years of singing, and it still sleeps. While my Choir sings, I do not stay down.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: Silence the Choir first. Everything every hold ever paid is in that organ. Let's give it back!

payload.title: The Keeper of the Great Anchor

nodes.speaker: class-cyclops02
nodes.line: Small. Warm. Loud. Keeper holds the big arch. Keeper came down with the shell and stayed to hold it. You are not allowed.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: Came down with the shell? So you fell out of the Manalith's own crust. And now you guard an Anchor.

nodes.speaker: class-cyclops02
nodes.line: Keeper does not remember. Keeper lifts a foot. Keeper stamps. Small things slide close to Keeper.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: When it lifts its foot, get clear, or stand ready. Whoever it drags in starts the first pincer.

payload.title: The Kiln Guard on the Stair

nodes.speaker: class-ceramicknight06
nodes.line: None climb to the cathedral. I was fired in the kiln for this stair. Side blows only scratch my glaze.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: Then we come at you top to bottom, and keep cracking until the porcelain gives.

nodes.speaker: class-mechaarmor01
nodes.line: CHOIR DIG. TITHED CREWS ONLY. TURN BACK. Look, kids, I just drive this thing for the Red Seal. Go home.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: Look at the crates, they're glowing. They're digging mana out of the Manalith's fallen shell.

nodes.speaker: class-mechaarmor01
nodes.line: SHIELD WALL ACTIVE. SIDE ASSAULTS WILL BE DEFLECTED. That's the card talking. The card's not wrong.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: Side hits glance off that shield. Pincer it top to bottom, or keep cracking it until it breaks.

nodes.speaker: class-moorcaptain
nodes.line: So you're the ones who broke my Collector's plate and drove off in my tithe wagon. Tithe paid its colour every month without a word until you came.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: Tithe paid because your man stood on the bridge with a prisoner. You sold the holds' tithe to the Choir. Your own people's.

nodes.speaker: class-moorcaptain
nodes.line: I sold it at quota. Without me the Choir takes three times that and nobody keeps the count. Give me room on my own moor and I strike twice.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: Then no room. Stay close to him, everyone. Never let the Captain end a turn alone.

nodes.speaker: class-oni02
nodes.line: The pass takes a toll. Leave the white wagon. This mask has fallen before. It always gets back up.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: Then we cut down its raiders first. With no one left standing beside it, that mask stays down.

nodes.speaker: class-chronomancer
nodes.line: Mind the floor. You came to see the tithe? Look in tank nine. That's a whole hold's colour, kept cold.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: A glow, cyan, tank after tank. That's mana, and far more than the Lullaby needs. Where does the rest go?

nodes.speaker: class-chronomancer
nodes.line: Up the spire. The Anchors sip, the spire drinks, and I keep the clocks. Give me room and I take two turns.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: Then no room. Close in on her, everyone. Someone stays beside her, every turn.

nodes.speaker: class-swampmistress00
nodes.line: Little drivers. This hull is mine. Halcyon built her to run from the sky, and the tide threw her here instead. The fen and I keep her now.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: It's a wreck in a swamp. Nobody's flying anything. You could walk away.

nodes.speaker: class-swampmistress00
nodes.line: And leave her to the Choir's salvage crews? My coven holds the mire for me. Strike at me and I'm simply somewhere else.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: She trades places with her coven. Cut them down first, and she has nowhere left to go.

nodes.speaker: character-aetherist
nodes.line: Back again? Mind the trays. The dust on them still remembers being part of something bigger.

choices.text: What is the dust, really?
Do you still sing?
Just passing through.

nodes.speaker: character-aetherist
nodes.line: Crust off the Manalith. Most of it's dead stone. A little still holds mana, and if you sing to it right, it gathers into a Shard instead of drifting home.

nodes.speaker: character-aetherist
nodes.line: Not their Lullaby. I sang that for the Choir until I saw where the surplus went. Now I only hum to the trays. They listen better.

nodes.speaker: character-aetherist
nodes.line: Go carefully. And bring me anything that glitters when the Manalith is up.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Back with more scrapes? Sit. Don't touch the green bottle.

choices.text: What's in the green bottle?
Just checking in.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Something that cures what the Shardfall does to blood. Mostly. Ask me again next week.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Drink water. Avoid the red rivers. Come back alive.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Gear holding up? Show me.

choices.text: Anything new on the anvil?
Just passing through.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Halcyon steel, off the walkers at the dig. Twelve hundred years old and still better than anything I can make. Humbling.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Keep your edge clean.

nodes.speaker: character-enchantress
nodes.line: The runes are restless tonight. So am I.

choices.text: What are the runes saying?
Get some rest.

nodes.speaker: character-enchantress
nodes.line: That the Manalith is closer than it was last month. They always say that. They're always right.

nodes.speaker: character-enchantress
nodes.line: Sleep well. I'll keep watch.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: There's soup on, and it's mostly vegetables. Mostly.

choices.text: Heard any news?
Smells good. Bye.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: The Captain's still looking for us. Someone in the last hold swore they saw the Manalith blink. People talk.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Don't let it get cold.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: What'll it be? Gossip's free, the rest isn't. A sellsword's contract runs three hundred gold.

choices.text: About that map I sold you.
About what I said on the road.
Hire us a sellsword.
Nothing today.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Still accurate, mostly. The roads move when the Manalith pulls. Trust the lanterns over the paper.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Water under the bridge. I've been called worse by better customers.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Paid, signed, sealed. One sellsword, as promised. Treat them well and they'll stay.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Come back when your purse is heavier.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Got a moment?

choices.text: How are you holding up?
What do you make of the merchant?
Get some rest.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Tired. Sore. Still here. That counts for something.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Sells us oil and sells us gossip. I trust the oil.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: You too. Somebody has to keep the fire going.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: That music is coming from the walls. I know this sound. We sang the Manalith to sleep with it.

nodes.speaker: character-enchantress
nodes.line: Your Lullaby. The Choir built the organ around it. The runaway says every hold's tithe ends in those pipes, and the Hierarch drinks the skim. The Lullaby needs a little. He takes the rest. Let's make it stop.

choices.text: Before we go in. You've got something to say.
We stop it. Today.

nodes.speaker: $trusted
nodes.line: Only this. Whatever you sang in that room long ago, you walked us here to end it. I go in beside you.

choices.text: Beside me, then. The first pipe we break, we break together.
Stay close in there. I'll need someone who knows my voice.

nodes.speaker: $trusted
nodes.line: Together. I'll be listening for it.

nodes.speaker: $trusted
nodes.line: I know it. I'd know it through a whole choir.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: The Watch's last captain knelt and gave me the chains, and they answered my hand. Why mine?

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Because only Halcyon's mana opens or closes them, and yours is the last of it. He held his post twelve hundred years for someone to hand them to. Every way this ends runs through you now. I'll forge whatever you need. You choose.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The wraith knights lowered their blades to me, then fought us anyway. And this arch hummed awake as I passed. What is it holding up?

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Nothing. The Street's engineer read the arch you woke: it's a tap, not a support. It draws the Manalith's mana down, and the drawing is the pull that brings it closer. The Watch knew you for one of Halcyon's. They saluted their own.

choices.text: You looked at me differently when the Watch saluted. Tell me why.
Halcyon's, then. I'd still rather know than guess.

nodes.speaker: $trusted
nodes.line: Because they saluted, and I didn't know if I should. Halcyon put the Manalith to sleep and drank the spill. Maybe you were one of them. I know who you've been out here. That's the one I'm following.

choices.text: Keep judging me by what I do out here. Hold me to it.
I don't know what I was either. I'm glad you're still here.

nodes.speaker: $trusted
nodes.line: I will. Every day, if I have to.

nodes.speaker: $trusted
nodes.line: Still here. Ask me again after the next arch.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Halt. That's a Choir wagon on Anchor ice. Give me one reason my hammer stays on my back.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The hammer is bigger than the one holding it, and it hasn't moved yet.

choices.text: Because we stole it.
Because you'd lose.
Because we're not here for you.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Stole it. From the Choir. Out here people don't steal from the Choir, they kneel to it and pay.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Ha. Plenty of things have told me that on this ice. The Watch's dead knights told me that. I'm still standing.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Nobody passes the arches by accident. Either you're carrying the tithe or you're running from it.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: My hold sent me to guard these arches. Every night they hum, and our tithe rides the beam up into the dark.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The arches throw their light at the sky.

choices.text: We ran from the tithe at Saltmoss. We're following the beams.
Guarding them for whom?

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Following them where? The beams go up. There's nothing up there but the stone in the sky.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: For my hold. For the oath. The Captain stood in our hall and swore the tithe would buy us peace. I swore to guard it.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: An oath is all a squire has. Why would I break mine for a stolen wagon and a story?

nodes.speaker: $party:2
nodes.line: It's no story. The Commander pulled the tithe out of the white wagon at Saltmoss, and the orb woke in their hand. Show them, Commander.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: An orb, awake, this close to the arches. The hum just changed. Listen. It's answering you.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The arch overhead hums lower, and the beam above it flickers.

choices.text: Your tithe goes up that beam. I mean to find out where.
The Captain sold your oath before you swore it.
Stand with us, and you won't stand alone.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Mine and my sister's and everyone's in the hold. I've watched it go up every night and never once asked where.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Careful. That's my hold you're talking about. But I've heard the Captain laugh in our hall, and it wasn't a laugh for us.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Standing alone is the whole job out here. You'd be surprised how heavy a hammer gets when nobody's beside you.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Saltmoss paid the same tithe as my hold. If somebody's finally asking where it goes, I want to be there for the answer.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: My shield is yours. I stand in front. It's what I'm for.

choices.text: Then stand in front, Knight. We'll stand behind you.
Thank the one who spoke for us.
Your oath was to the hold. Don't forget it was the Captain who took it.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Behind me is the safest place on this ice. Stay there and we'll get along fine.

nodes.speaker: $party:2
nodes.line: You were going to swing that hammer. I'd rather it swung for us.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Then it will. A hold knight remembers a debt like that. I'll keep you behind my shield.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: I won't forget. I'll hold that oath against the Captain when we meet. Just don't ask me to like hearing it.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: The organ's broken and the Underspire's lights are brighter than ever. What are they burning?

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Halcyon's taps. Our runner wires those signs herself: every lamp down here drinks from the lines that pull the Manalith closer. Three crews want the empty spire, and every one has asked after you by name.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The archive woke for me. A council, a vote, a row of commanders. One of those faces was mine.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: The witch read it while you stared. Halcyon couldn't stop the Manalith, so it fed it to sleep and drank what spilled. Every scrap of mana in us is the Manalith's. And you were in that room. I'm still deciding what I think of that.

choices.text: And you? You saw that face as well.
Take the time you need. I'm still deciding too.

nodes.speaker: $trusted
nodes.line: I've decided. A face on a wall is who you were. I've watched who you are. If that council made you, you've spent every day since unmaking it. I'll stand with the one I've watched.

choices.text: Then watch me closely. If I start turning into that face, stop me.
Thank you. That's more than I'd give myself today.

nodes.speaker: $trusted
nodes.line: I'll stop you. Then I'll drag you back to the fire and we'll talk.

nodes.speaker: $trusted
nodes.line: Then take mine until you can give it yourself.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Sit down. You brought the Still's cold out with you. I can see it on your skin.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The healer is already reaching for a satchel of salves.

choices.text: Thank you. We'll sit.
We don't have time to sit.
Who are you?

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Good. Most people down here argue first and sit after they fall over. Hands out. Let me see.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Then you have time to fall over. Sit, or I'll be mending you off the floor in an hour.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Somebody who mends people. Down here that's all anybody needs to know about me, and more than most ask.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The salve is warm, and smells of lantern oil.

choices.text: That's Lantern Road oil. You're far from the gorges.
Why mend strangers under the spire?

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: You know the road. Then you know the lanterns burn on mana, same as the neon up there. I came to see what the city does with it.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Because nobody else does. The Street patches its own and the Choir patches nobody. Somebody has to mend the rest.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: I counted the pilgrims who climbed the stair to the top of the spire. None came down. Now you mean to climb it too.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Tell me why I should send three more up that stair with my salve still wet on them.

nodes.speaker: $party:2
nodes.line: Because the Commander came out of the Still, and the orbs wake when they're near. We've been mended by worse hands than yours, and we're still walking.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Out of the Still. That's why the cold won't leave your skin. And the orb in your hand is glowing like a lantern.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The light in the orb pulses, slow as a heartbeat.

choices.text: Whatever's at the top drinks the tithe. We mean to stop it.
Walk with us, and nobody climbs alone.
Where we're going is worse than this.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Whatever drinks at the top of that spire has drunk enough. I've buried enough pilgrims to say so.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Nobody climbs alone. The road says that over every lantern. I didn't think I'd hear it under the spire.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Worse than a stair nobody comes down? Then you'll need somebody at the back who means to come down again.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: If your wagon has no seat left, I'll walk behind it with the satchel and come forward when somebody bleeds.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Then I'll mend you on the way up. A healer at the back is still a healer.

choices.text: Glad to have you, Sage.
Thank the one who vouched for us.
Your salve is welcome. Your doubts can stay down here.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Glad to be had. Now hold still, the cold's not out of you yet.

nodes.speaker: $party:2
nodes.line: Someone had to. And I could use the mending, after the Still.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Then you're first in line. Sit. The road looks after the ones who speak up for it.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: My doubts come with me. They're what kept me off the stair. I'll mend you anyway.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: By the wagon wheel the Cleric has a roll of clean bandage out and is holding it toward the Barbarian, who has both fists tucked under both arms like a child hiding sweets.

nodes.speaker: class-cleric
nodes.line: Your knuckles are split to the bone and you're wrapping them in that. Choir white, off a tithe wagon, that's been on a dozen cuts. Let me do it properly.

nodes.speaker: class-barbarian
nodes.line: The white's mine. I bleed on it on purpose. And you were the one I couldn't tell from the slime, that day the red came up on me. You stood there. Why'd you stand there?

nodes.speaker: class-cleric
nodes.line: Because I've stood closer to worse. I wore that white, Barbarian. Six years at the tables. I don't know if I was ever at Saltmoss. I never learned the places. Only the people.

choices.text: The Cleric walked away from the tables. That's the side that counts.
Neither of you put anyone in that chair. The Choir did.
That's between the two of you. I won't take a side on it.
When the red comes, I shout Saltmoss. Let the Cleric shout it too.

nodes.speaker: class-barbarian
nodes.line: Easy for you to say, Commander. You weren't sat by the door all winter. But aye. Walked away. That's more than the collector at our well ever did.

nodes.speaker: class-barbarian
nodes.line: The Choir. Aye. It's a big word to hate. Easier to hate one face. I'll try the big word for a while.

nodes.speaker: class-barbarian
nodes.line: Fine. We'll sort it ourselves, then. We usually do.

nodes.speaker: class-barbarian
nodes.line: Saltmoss, from a healer's mouth. Huh. If you shout it, I'll know it's meant. Nobody shouts that word by accident.

nodes.speaker: class-cleric
nodes.line: I keep a book of names. If there's anyone from Saltmoss in it, I'd like you to know who. If there isn't, I'd like to write someone down. You choose who.

choices.text: Look through it together, both of you, by the same lamp.
Ash. Write Ash in it, as a living name and not a lost one.
Tell the Barbarian about Wren.
Some books are better left shut tonight.

nodes.speaker: class-barbarian
nodes.line: Same lamp. Go on, then. Read me the names slow. I'm not much for reading, but I'll know a Saltmoss name when I hear one.

nodes.speaker: class-barbarian
nodes.line: Living. Aye. Write it big. A-S-H. Not in the back with the lost ones. Up front, where you'd put someone you were going to see again.

nodes.speaker: class-barbarian
nodes.line: Twelve, and she asked if the colour went somewhere nice. Moors take it. Give me the bandage, Cleric. I'll wear it under the white, if that's how you want it.

nodes.speaker: class-barbarian
nodes.line: Shut's fine. I've no head for names tonight. My hands, though. You can have my hands.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Barbarian holds out both fists. The Cleric wraps them in clean linen, then winds the white cloth back over the top, turn by turn, and ties it off with steady fingers.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Engineer has a smashed Halcyon housing in pieces on a cloth, fitting the shards together. The Barbarian, who smashed it, is eating a cold potato and pretending not to watch.

nodes.speaker: class-engineer
nodes.line: This was a seal housing. Halcyon. Older than the Choir, possibly older than the road. I had seven questions for it. Now I've got a puzzle with no corners.

nodes.speaker: class-barbarian
nodes.line: It was shooting at the Cleric. Things that shoot at the Cleric get hit. That's my whole list of questions.

nodes.speaker: class-engineer
nodes.line: I'm not saying don't hit it. I'm saying hit it there, on the collar, not in the middle where the good parts are. Is that so much to ask?

choices.text: The Engineer calls the spot, the Barbarian hits it. That's a plan.
In a fight, the Barbarian doesn't stop to take notes. Neither should you.
Argue this before the fight, both of you, not after.
Learn the word. Saltmoss. If the red's up and you need a spot hit, shout that first.

nodes.speaker: class-barbarian
nodes.line: You shout, I swing. Aye. Shout loud. And don't shout "collar". I don't know which end's the collar.

nodes.speaker: class-engineer
nodes.line: Notes are how I keep the lights on, Commander. Fine. I'll take them after. From the bits.

nodes.speaker: class-barbarian
nodes.line: Before. Over supper. With drawings, I suppose. Go on, then. Draw me a collar.

nodes.speaker: class-engineer
nodes.line: Saltmoss, then "collar". I'm writing that down. Page forty. You're on page forty now, Barbarian, with the good questions.

nodes.speaker: class-barbarian
nodes.line: Somebody back home wants you square, I hear. When we get near your old city, I stand behind you. Close enough to be seen.

choices.text: We said the crew pays the debt together. The Barbarian's crew.
Redline gets nothing. Let them see the Barbarian and do the sum.
No fists in the Underspire. That's an order.
Behind, then. Not in front. It's the Engineer's debt to close.

nodes.speaker: class-engineer
nodes.line: Together. Redline sends letters on red wire and counts in fish. I'd like to see the sum when a whole crew walks in, and this one at the back.

nodes.speaker: class-engineer
nodes.line: Do the sum. Ha. Redline's good at sums. They'll get to the Barbarian and stop counting.

nodes.speaker: class-barbarian
nodes.line: No fists. I heard. I'll stand there with my hands in my pockets and look at them, then. Nobody ever ordered me not to look.

nodes.speaker: class-engineer
nodes.line: My debt to close. Yes. But it's a lot easier to close with somebody standing where they can see you. Thank you, Barbarian.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Engineer pushes a shard across the cloth. The Barbarian picks it up, turns it the wrong way, then the right way, and it fits.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Knight's shield lies face up by the fire with a fresh axe-bite in the rim. The Barbarian put it there, and the Knight has not stopped looking at it.

nodes.speaker: class-knight
nodes.line: You went through my line today. Straight through it. You're meant to be behind the shield, not on the other side of it swinging back.

nodes.speaker: class-barbarian
nodes.line: I've never been behind anyone. Not at home, not on the moors. First in. That's what I'm for.

nodes.speaker: class-knight
nodes.line: First in is what I'm for. Stand before the hold. It's cut in the rim, next to your axe mark. So which of us goes first, Commander? You decide, and we'll both hate it.

choices.text: The Knight. The shield's made for it. The Barbarian goes second and hits harder for the wait.
The Barbarian. The Knight covers the flank.
Side by side. Shield and axe on the same step.
The oath was to the hold, not the hall. The Barbarian's part of the hold now.

nodes.speaker: class-barbarian
nodes.line: Second. Fine. But if I see the shield go down, I'm not waiting for permission.

nodes.speaker: class-knight
nodes.line: The flank. Fine. It's a good flank. I'll keep it, and I'll keep my opinions about it, too.

nodes.speaker: class-knight
nodes.line: Same step. That's not in any drill I ever learned. We'll practise it. You'll keep time badly.

nodes.speaker: class-knight
nodes.line: Part of the hold. The well children would have run from you. Then they'd have followed you everywhere. All right. Before the hold means before you too.

nodes.speaker: class-barbarian
nodes.line: Your Captain sold your hold to the beam. My collector laughed at the well. If we ever get there and that Captain's in the hall, what then?

choices.text: We go to the Knight's sister first. Both of you at her door.
Neither of you swings at the Captain without my word.
Then the Captain sees both of you coming, and does the sum.
Stand beside the ones who stand. You cut it yourself. That's the Barbarian.

nodes.speaker: class-knight
nodes.line: My sister will take one look at you and hand you a bucket. That's how she says welcome. Carry it up from the well, and she'll never forget your name.

nodes.speaker: class-barbarian
