I'm not choosing between your homes over a stew. Work it out.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: A vote. Fine. And when mine wins, you're scrubbing both pots.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: The rest of it. All right. What do your people put in for the sour?

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Worked out it is. Hand me the spoon. Last, a pinch at a time.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: You know, I was told your people were cold. Proud, and not much for sharing a fire.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: I was told the same of yours. Nobody told me you'd fight this hard over salt.

choices.text: Whoever told you both was a long way from this fire.
Keep the stories. Just don't let them choose who you stand beside.
Some of those stories are true. Keep your guard up.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: A long way. Aye. They never sat at a pot with you.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: We'll keep them for the jokes, then. And stand where we like.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Guard up. I've had it up so long I barely notice it any more.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: Two pots go on the fire. Later, the whole camp tastes both, and the argument starts over, louder, and more friendly.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: Two of the caravan's heroes have pulled their bedrolls close tonight. They grew up under the same banner, and it shows in small ways: the same knot in a boot lace, the same way of banking a fire.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: You bank it the way we did back home. Ash on the windward side, so the wind can't get under it. I haven't seen anyone do that in years.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Nobody else here does it right. I fix the others' fires when they aren't looking.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Commander, we came from the same place and never once met there. You'd think we'd have crossed paths a hundred times.

choices.text: Home's big. You found each other out here. That's what counts.
Then trade it back and forth. The streets, the songs, the people.
Old loyalties get in the way on the road. Don't lean on them.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Out past every map we grew up with. Aye. That's something.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Start with the bakery by the gate, then. If you knew the bakery, you knew everyone.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: We won't lean. But we'll still bank the fire the right way.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: The collectors came through twice a year. I always wondered who else stood in the square while they read the names out.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: I did. Every time. We might have stood a shoulder apart and never known it.

choices.text: Next time a collector reads a name, you'll stand together on purpose.
That square is behind you both now.
Some memories are better left in the square.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: On purpose. Aye. Shoulder to shoulder, and loud about it.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Behind us. It doesn't feel like it some nights. Tonight it does.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Left, then. Pass the salt, and we'll talk about something lighter.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The two of them fall to arguing over the name of a hill outside home, and neither will give it up, and both are smiling.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: Behind the wagons the Striker is drawing lines in the dirt with a stick, and the Mage is rubbing them out with a boot as fast as they go down.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Every fight you run into my circle half a breath before it closes. Half a breath. I've held a spell back three times this week for you.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: And three times the thing in the circle was still standing because you waited. If I don't go in, it walks out of your circle and onto whoever's behind us.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Commander, one of us is going to get the other killed. I'd rather it was settled out here, with a stick.

choices.text: Call it out loud. The Mage says the count, the Striker goes on the last word.
The Mage casts on time, every time. The Striker learns the circle.
Hold back, both of you. I'll call every fight myself.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: A count. Three, two, and I'm gone on one. I can hear a count over anything.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Learn the circle. All right. Draw it for me again, slower, and don't rub it out this time.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Then we wait on you every time. Fine. But the fights won't.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: The truth is, I've never had anyone fast enough to be in the circle at all. Most people run away from it.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Running away from a spell is sense. Running into one is trust. You've never once dropped it on me.

choices.text: That's the closest thing to a promise either of you has made. Keep it.
Trust is good. Practice is better. Again tomorrow, at first light.
Don't make it sound grander than it is. It's timing.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Then here's mine. I'll never close the circle while you're inside it. Not once.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: First light. Bring the stick. I'll bring the feet.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Timing, then. Mine's good. Yours is getting there.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Mage draws one more circle in the dirt. This time the Striker stands in the middle of it, grinning, and the Mage counts aloud, slowly, down to one.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Support has been up before everyone again: boots oiled, water skins filled, a spare strap laid by every bedroll. Tonight one hero is still awake to catch the Support at it.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: So it's you. Every morning my gear's better than I left it. I thought the caravan had a ghost.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: A ghost would do it better. I just don't sleep much. And a loose strap in a fight is worse than any blade.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Nobody thanks you for it. I've never heard anyone say a word. Commander, have you?

choices.text: I've seen it. I should have said so sooner. Thank you, both of you, for noticing.
Then say it now. It means more from the one whose straps got fixed.
The Support doesn't do it for thanks. Leave it be.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Noticing's plenty. More than plenty. I'd go on doing it either way.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Thank you, then. For the straps, and the boots, and whatever else I never caught.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Maybe not. But it should still be said.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: You want to know the truth? I watch you in a fight, every time. When you stumble, I'm already moving. It's easier when I know someone's watching back.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Then I'll watch back. Every fight. And some mornings, I'll be up first.

choices.text: Up first together. Two pairs of hands, half the time.
Watch back, yes. But let the Support sleep in once in a while.
Your own gear is your own work. Look to that first.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Half the time. I don't know what I'll do with the other half. Sleep, maybe.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Sleep in. That'd be something. I'll try it once and see if the caravan falls apart.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: My own gear. Fine. But I'm still saying thank you.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: Before dawn, two figures move between the bedrolls with oil and spare straps, whispering, and the work is done in half the time.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Healer sits beside the Tank with a lamp and a needle, closing the last cut of the day. Neither says much. They've done this many times now.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Eleven today. I count them, every one. Eleven blows that would have landed on someone else if you hadn't stepped in front.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: That's the work. You stand at the back and keep us breathing. I stand at the front and keep them busy. It's a fair trade.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: It isn't fair. You take the wound and I take the thanks. Commander, tell the Tank to stop stepping in front of everything.

choices.text: The Tank stands there because the Healer is behind. That's the whole trust between you.
Fewer steps forward, then. I'd rather the Tank whole for the next fight.
Counting wounds won't help anyone. Let it go.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Behind me. Aye. I don't look back to check. I never have to.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Fewer. I can try fewer. Not none.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: I can't let it go. It's the only way I know what you cost.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Here. You've been saying the count out loud for weeks. Mark it somewhere, if you need it marked. On the shield, where I'll see it.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: On the shield. A notch for every one I closed.

choices.text: Do it. Let the shield carry what the two of you carry.
Mark the ones you both came home from, not the wounds.
A shield is no ledger. Keep it clean.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Eleven, then. Start tonight. I'll wear the count into every fight.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: The ones we came home from. That's a better count. That one I'd like to see grow.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Clean it stays. The count can live with you, then. I trust you to keep it.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The lamp burns low. The Healer ties off the last stitch, and the Tank flexes the arm and calls it good as new, which it isn't, quite.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: It is past the middle of the night. The Knight is still on watch at the edge of the firelight, shield grounded, and the Sage has come out with a blanket and a cup and no intention of going back.

nodes.speaker: class-sage
nodes.line: That's your third watch running, Knight. On the road we'd call that a slow knot. Not tied yet. Just a matter of time.

nodes.speaker: class-knight
nodes.line: I'll sleep when the road's quiet. It isn't. There's something two hills back that keeps not quite following us. Somebody has to stand before the camp.

nodes.speaker: class-sage
nodes.line: Somebody. Not the same somebody every night. A tired shield is a door left open. Commander, you're the one the Knight listens to.

choices.text: The Knight sleeps tonight. The Sage takes the watch.
Split it. Half the night each, and sit together at the change.
The Knight keeps the watch. That's what the shield is for.
I took the Knight's watch once, the way the Knight took it for us at the ford. Now the Sage takes it.

nodes.speaker: class-knight
nodes.line: Fine. The shield stays here, by your foot, and you wake me if anything on that hill so much as coughs. Promise, Sage.

nodes.speaker: class-sage
nodes.line: Half each. I'll take the second half. Healers are good at the hour before dawn. That's when people need us.

nodes.speaker: class-sage
nodes.line: Then I'll sit here and keep the watch company. You can't order me to bed, Knight. You're not the Commander.

nodes.speaker: class-knight
nodes.line: The ford. I'd nearly forgotten that was the same thing. All right. Two watches to give back, then, and I'll take the third.

nodes.speaker: class-knight
nodes.line: You've a clean end to tie on that cord, and I've a second line on the rim I can't get past the first word of. Both of us stuck at the last bit. Do you ever think we're afraid to finish?

choices.text: No knots for anyone here. The Knight stands before, so the cord stays clean.
When we reach the holds, the Sage looks at the sister first, before anyone.
Trade. The Sage helps pick the Knight's second line. The Knight helps pick the last knot.
Those ends are each of yours to finish alone.

nodes.speaker: class-sage
nodes.line: A clean cord because there's a shield in front of it. I'll take that. But you sleep sometimes, Knight. A shield on its face in the mud covers nobody.

nodes.speaker: class-sage
nodes.line: First. A water carrier, you said. I'll know her colour before she's set the bucket down. And then I'll want to meet the stubborn one with the spears in the well.

nodes.speaker: class-knight
nodes.line: You pick my word, I pick your knot. That's a fair trade. Fair warning, Sage, I'll pick something plain. Holds don't do fancy.

nodes.speaker: class-knight
nodes.line: Alone. Yes. Some things are. I'll stand my watch, and you count your knots, and we'll both pretend we're not counting each other.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The blanket ends up round both their shoulders. The Knight's shield stays grounded between them, and the thing two hills back never does follow.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Engineer is lying on one elbow a careful arm's length from the Red Mage's tin, holding a brass gauge on a chain and not quite pointing it at the coal.

nodes.speaker: class-engineer
nodes.line: Nine years, you said. A coal doesn't last nine nights, not without feeding. You feed it peat, I've watched. That doesn't add up. Something in there is wrong in a way I'd like to understand.

nodes.speaker: class-redmage
nodes.line: Nothing in there is wrong. It's my aunt's hearth. Put the brass away before I melt it into a ring for you.

nodes.speaker: class-engineer
nodes.line: I'm not trying to take it. Halcyon seals run warm for a hundred years on nothing. If your coal does the same, that's a question with an answer. Commander, tell the Red Mage I'm harmless.

choices.text: Let the Engineer measure it. Gauge only. The lid stays where the Red Mage puts it.
Ask the Red Mage, not the tin. The coal answers to one person.
A fire near the wagons is everyone's business. Measure it, Engineer.
I let the Engineer open the orb, and nothing broke. A gauge on a tin is less than that.

nodes.speaker: class-redmage
nodes.line: Gauge only. Fine. If that needle so much as twitches toward the lid, Engineer, I'm keeping it. Well? What does it say?

nodes.speaker: class-engineer
nodes.line: Ask. All right. Red Mage, may I? Please? I've a whole page for it. Page sixty. It's been empty since the fen.

nodes.speaker: class-redmage
nodes.line: Everyone's business. It's been my business alone for nine years and the wagons are still here. Measure, then. I'll be over there, not watching.

nodes.speaker: class-redmage
nodes.line: The orb. And it's still glowing, I suppose. Fine. One look. One. My aunt would have liked you, Engineer. She liked people who asked first.

nodes.speaker: class-engineer
nodes.line: It reads like a seal. Old warmth, not fire warmth. Tap Seven ran like this until it didn't, and Redline put that on my account. If your coal is the same thing, it's worth more than the fish market.

choices.text: Redline gets nothing, and the coal isn't for sale. Say it together and mean it.
The coal goes home to the aunt's hearth. Build it a grate that will hold it.
Build the Red Mage a better tin. Vented, hinged, and never opened by anyone else.
Whatever it's worth, it stays a coal. No more questions about it.

nodes.speaker: class-redmage
nodes.line: Nothing. Not one ember. If Redline asks, Engineer, tell them it went out years ago. I'll look very sad.

nodes.speaker: class-engineer
nodes.line: A grate. Iron, not brass, brass goes soft. Draw me the hearth, Red Mage, and I'll have the fitting ready by the time we pass the fens.

nodes.speaker: class-engineer
nodes.line: Double-walled. Vent in the lid, latch only you can work. I'll make the latch backwards. Nobody ever thinks to try it backwards.

nodes.speaker: class-engineer
nodes.line: No more questions. Page sixty stays half full, then. That's harder for me than it sounds, Commander.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The gauge goes back on its chain. The Red Mage turns the tin a little toward the Engineer, so the light from the dent falls on the open notebook.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: After the ford the Knight sits with the shield across both knees, working the strap buckle with fingers gone white and slow. The Red Mage watches from across the fire and has already pulled one glove off.

nodes.speaker: class-redmage
nodes.line: You've been at that buckle since the water. Your fingers aren't working, Knight. Give them here. I can have them warm before the kettle is.

nodes.speaker: class-knight
nodes.line: In the holds, you warm your own hands or you lose them. Nobody puts heat into you. It goes in one door and out another, and then there's two cold people.

nodes.speaker: class-redmage
nodes.line: I know how heat goes in and doesn't stay. I did that for a whole winter. This isn't that. This is a buckle and a pair of hands. Commander, tell the Knight to hold still.

choices.text: Hold your hands out, Knight. The Red Mage knows exactly how much.
Warm the shield, not the Knight. Iron keeps heat longer than skin.
The Knight's fine. Red Mage, keep your fire for the field.
We said fire would be tried together, never alone. Try it here, with the Knight.

nodes.speaker: class-knight
nodes.line: Fine. Fine. There. That's, huh. That's not a fire at all. That's like a hearth through a wall. You've done this before, Red Mage.

nodes.speaker: class-redmage
nodes.line: Iron, then. Hold the rim. Not the face, I won't touch the old line. There. Now when you grip, it gives the heat back slowly.

nodes.speaker: class-knight
nodes.line: The field. Right. Thank you anyway, Red Mage. I'll sit closer to the kettle. That much I can manage myself.

nodes.speaker: class-redmage
nodes.line: Together. Then you tell me when it's enough, Knight. That's the part I never had. Someone telling me when to stop.

nodes.speaker: class-redmage
nodes.line: While I've got you. When we fight, I'm the one nearest whatever's burning, and the tin rides on my coat. If I go down, it goes in the mud. You stand behind that shield all day. Would you carry it?

choices.text: Beside, not in front. The tin rides between the two of you.
It's going home to the aunt's hearth. Knight, see it gets there whatever happens to the rest of us.
The Knight carries it. Nothing gets past that shield.
It stays on the Red Mage. Some things you don't hand over.

nodes.speaker: class-knight
nodes.line: Between us. I like that better than in front. Strap it to my belt on your side, Red Mage, and stay where you can reach it.

nodes.speaker: class-knight
nodes.line: To the hearth. I've carried worse promises over worse ground. If the tin and I get there alone, I'll knock and say who sent me.

nodes.speaker: class-redmage
nodes.line: Behind the shield. It's never been out of my reach in nine years. I'll hate every minute. Don't drop it, Knight. Don't you dare.

nodes.speaker: class-knight
nodes.line: Then I'll stand where the tin is. Same thing, from my side. Keep your coat buttoned, Red Mage.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The buckle comes loose on the next try. The Knight sets the shield down on the Red Mage's side of the fire, face up, close enough to catch the warmth.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Sage has the satchel open and a jar of something green in one hand, and keeps looking at the back of the Red Mage's ungloved hand as if it were a wound still open.

nodes.speaker: class-redmage
nodes.line: They're healed, Sage. Years ago. You can stop measuring them by eye. I can see you doing it.

nodes.speaker: class-sage
nodes.line: Healed isn't the same as mended. That skin's tight as a drum. It pulls when you make a fist, doesn't it? This jar won't take the marks away, but it'll give you your grip back.

nodes.speaker: class-redmage
nodes.line: I did these to myself. On purpose. I'm not sure I want good salve spent on them. Commander, tell the Sage to put the lid back on.

choices.text: Let the Sage tend them. Tonight, the glove stays off.
Trade. The Red Mage warms the Sage's jars on cold mornings. The Sage keeps the hand supple.
Scars are the Red Mage's own business. Put the jar away.
The aunt asked the Red Mage to stop, for the Red Mage's own sake. Let the Sage finish what she asked.

nodes.speaker: class-sage
nodes.line: Hold still. Cold first, then it warms. You of all people will feel the turn. There. Make a fist. Slowly.

nodes.speaker: class-redmage
nodes.line: Warm jars. That I can do without thinking. Your salves set like candle wax by dawn, Sage. I've watched you chip at them.

nodes.speaker: class-sage
nodes.line: Away it goes. I'll leave it at the top of the satchel. Jars don't mind waiting. Healers do, but we're used to it.

nodes.speaker: class-redmage
nodes.line: She did ask. For my sake. Not because it hurt, because she could see me hoping. Go on, then, Sage. Before I think better of it.

nodes.speaker: class-sage
nodes.line: Your aunt went Hollow at the tithe. Wick's colour went thin in the city, a little more each week. Same Choir, I think. Different doors. I don't know what to do with that, Red Mage. Do you?

choices.text: We promised to bring Wick down. The aunt comes into that promise too.
The coal goes home to the aunt's hearth. The Sage walks it there with the Red Mage.
Compare everything. Every jar the Sage tried, every night the Red Mage tried. Two lists are better than one.
Different doors. Don't make one grief out of two.

nodes.speaker: class-redmage
nodes.line: The same promise. Wick and her both. That's a bigger stair than it was this morning, Sage. Good. I wanted a reason to climb faster.

nodes.speaker: class-sage
nodes.line: The hearth. I'd like to meet a coal that's outlasted every jar in this satchel. And the person who lit it.

nodes.speaker: class-redmage
nodes.line: Every night. I can give you every night. How much heat, how long, what she said. I never wrote any of it down. I remember all of it.

nodes.speaker: class-sage
nodes.line: Two griefs. You're right. I'd only have made yours fit the shape of mine. That's a healer's worst habit.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The jar ends up open on the stone between them. The Red Mage holds it near the fire until the salve goes soft, and passes it back without being asked.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: The shell's still breaking, and the whole red host is marching north. Toward the arches. My people's arches.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Our deserter knows the banners. His own kin lead the march: open every tap at once and drag the Manalith down, the way their creed always wanted. If they reach the Anchors first, the sky decides for all of us.

nodes.speaker: character-aetherist
nodes.line: Don't step on the trays! Every grain on them took me a day to sift out of the sand.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: You're sifting the Shardfall? The Choir punishes anyone who steals from its dig.

nodes.speaker: character-aetherist
nodes.line: Then it's a good thing I'm leaving. You have a wagon and I have a trade: bring me dust, I'll make you Shards. Room for one more?

choices.text: Climb on. We could use a trade.
How do you make Shards out of dust?

nodes.speaker: character-aetherist
nodes.line: I sing to it. I learned the Lullaby in the Cathedral's lower choir, then learned to sing it backwards. It makes the mana gather instead of drain.

nodes.speaker: character-aetherist
nodes.line: Then I'll set my trays by your fire. Keep bringing me dust and I'll keep you in Shards.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Careful where you step. I've got a whole batch drying on those rocks.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: A splice-cutter? Out here?

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Someone has to study what the red rivers do. I could use a wagon. Mind if I come along?

choices.text: Climb on.
Is it safe?

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Safer than leaving me here. I'll keep you patched up.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Here, take this bottle. You'll need it sooner than you think.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: See this? Shardfall sand, fired with a sliver of shell. It comes out as glass, and the glass remembers the heat. It remembers anything you pour through it.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: Can it remember an edge? We're losing blades faster than we find them.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Give me a crucible and a few quiet nights at camp. Bring me shards and steel, and I'll find out what they'll take.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: Red earth, and horns taller than towers. Did these fall? My hand aches when I go near them.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Some of them are the Manalith's own shell, shed as it comes. The Choir digs it out and the Ember pray for the rest. And that ache is your mana answering. Everyone's runs thin. Yours is whole. I've never seen that.

choices.text: You've watched my hand all morning. Say it.
Whole, and I don't know why. Let's keep moving.

nodes.speaker: $trusted
nodes.line: The ache. I've seen people go near a shard and come back thin. You come back steadier. I don't understand it, and I don't need to. I just want to be close when it matters.

choices.text: Stay close, then. If my hand starts to shake, you'll be the one I tell.
Stay near. Whatever this is, I'd rather not find out alone.

nodes.speaker: $trusted
nodes.line: The one you tell. I'll hold you to that, Commander.

nodes.speaker: $trusted
nodes.line: Not alone. That's an easy promise to keep.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Hey! White wagon! Don't run me down, I'm not with the Choir. I just look this dusty.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: You're a long way from the Underspire. What are you doing out in the red?

choices.text: Climb aboard. Explain on the way.
It's rough out here.
Who left you out here?

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Not so fast. I don't climb into anything I haven't looked under first.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Rough? The Choir's dig hired me to fix their walkers, then stiffed me. They're cracking the Manalith's fallen shell open out there.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: The Choir's dig. Hired me to keep their walkers walking, paid me in blessings, and left me a canteen and a direction.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Your axle's cracked, by the way. And there's an orb bolted under the bench that's humming. Those don't hum. Nothing from Halcyon hums anymore.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Engineer is already halfway under the wagon.

choices.text: It does that near me.
Can you fix the axle?

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Near you. Step back. Further. It's gone quiet. Come closer. It's humming again. That's not possible, and I'd like to take it apart.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Of course I can fix the axle. The question is whether you can pay better than the Choir did.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Engineer waits, wrench in hand.

choices.text: Water, and a ride out of the red.
Nothing yet. But we won't leave you stranded.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Water is the only coin out here that nobody fakes. Done.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Everyone says that. The Choir said it. Still, you stopped the wagon, which is more than they did.

nodes.speaker: $party:2
nodes.line: It's not only the bench orb. In a fight our orbs wake around the Commander. Every one of them.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Every orb in a fight? The dig would kill for that. They're breaking open a fallen shell for a fraction of it.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Commander looks out over the red, toward the dig.

choices.text: Then come keep it out of their hands.
The Ember will want it too.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: The Ember? Then you're driving the whitest wagon in the red past the people who burn white things. You'll need it to run faster than it does.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Deal. I'll fix your axle on the move. And keep the wagon moving. The Ember hates anything white.

choices.text: Welcome aboard, Engineer.
Thank the one who vouched for us.
Fix the axle first. The orb can wait.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Aboard and under it. Wake me if anything else starts humming.

nodes.speaker: $party:2
nodes.line: I only said what I saw. You'd have climbed under the wagon either way.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Probably. But it's nice to be asked for once, instead of hired.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Fine. Axle first. But I'm keeping a list of questions, and it's getting long.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: Night, a day's ride past Saltmoss. The stolen tithe wagon stands in a ring of gorse with its white paint already scraped with mud, and the three who ran with the Commander sit around a fire they are afraid to make any bigger.

nodes.speaker: $party:1
nodes.line: The Captain's riders turned back at the ford. They'll be out again at first light, with more of them. Before then I'd like to know who I just stole a wagon for.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The orb at the Commander's belt brightens a little in the dark, as it has since the dead lantern in Saltmoss lit again.

choices.text: The truth, then. I died in the Still, a long time ago, and woke there this morning.
I don't know much more than you do. My memory comes back in pieces.
Someone the Choir wants back. That should be enough for tonight.

nodes.speaker: $party:2
nodes.line: Died. In the Still. And walked out. Every child on the moors has a story about that vault, and none of them end with somebody walking out.

nodes.speaker: $party:1
nodes.line: Pieces. Fine. I'll take a straight answer with holes in it over a whole one that's lying.

nodes.speaker: $party:3
nodes.line: Good. What we don't know, the Captain can't squeeze out of us. Keep the rest until we're somewhere with walls.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: Someone has to sit up with the fire while the others sleep.

choices.text: Knight. You put yourself between the riders and the wagon at the ford. The watch is yours.
Barbarian. You'll hear them coming before any of us. Take the watch.
Cleric, you've mended every cut since the ford. Sleep. Someone else can watch tonight.
I'll take the first watch myself. None of you asked for any of this.

nodes.speaker: class-knight
nodes.line: Gladly. A wall that sleeps isn't much of a wall. Rest, all of you. Nothing comes over that ridge without going through me first.

nodes.speaker: class-barbarian
nodes.line: Good. I'd not have slept anyway, not in a Choir wagon with the Captain's dogs on our scent. If anything moves out there, you'll hear me before you hear it.

nodes.speaker: class-cleric
nodes.line: Kind of you to notice. Healers get thanked after the fight, hardly ever before it. I'll sleep, but wake me if anyone so much as sneezes.

nodes.speaker: $party:3
nodes.line: A commander who stands watch. Where I'm from, the ones giving orders sleep warm. I'll sit up with you a while anyway.

nodes.speaker: $party:2
nodes.line: At first light we run hard down the moor road. It's fast, and every hour we stay near Saltmoss is an hour the Captain gets closer.

nodes.speaker: $party:3
nodes.line: And every rider the Captain has knows that road. The peat cuts are slow, but no white wagon has ever gone that way. Nobody would think to look.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: Both of them look to the Commander.

choices.text: We take the road, and we take it fast.
The peat cuts. Slow and unseen beats fast and caught.
Neither of you is wrong. The road by night, the cuts by day.

nodes.speaker: $party:2
nodes.line: That's the answer I wanted. Get the wheels greased; we're gone before the frost lifts.

nodes.speaker: $party:3
nodes.line: Then pack light. The peat swallows anything heavy, and I'd rather it didn't swallow us.

nodes.speaker: $party:1
nodes.line: Riding at night with a stolen wagon. Either that's very clever or we'll find out soon that it isn't.

nodes.speaker: $party:1
nodes.line: Whatever we are now, a crew, a caravan, a band of thieves, we're it. We may as well make a proper camp of it.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: By the time the fire burns low there is a pit dug for it, a lookout on the ridge and a wagon nobody calls stolen any more. It is the first Camp.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: Walls on every hold, and the Captain's colours still on the gate. The Choir's gone. Who is he collecting for now?

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Himself. The knight who rode with us swore her oath to that hold, and he sold it out from under her. And at every gate I trade at, someone asks me a price. Not for the spire. For you.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: You're the innkeeper from Saltmoss. You followed us?

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Somebody had to. You stole the tithe wagon with no food and no plan.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: I'll cook, you fight. Fair?

choices.text: Fair.
How much will it cost us?

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Less than starving. Feed me and I'll feed you.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Good. Now, who's peeling the potatoes?

payload.title: A lantern that should be dead

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Tithe Moors. Every hold has paid, and the white wagons still come. I don't know these hills. I don't know why I'm walking them.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Three times the quota this year, and nobody says why. And that lantern on the caravan had been dead longer than my grandmother. It lit in your hand. So when you remember who you are, I'd like to hear it.

choices.text: You've been quiet by the wagon. Say what you're thinking.
When I remember, you'll be the first to hear it.

nodes.speaker: $trusted
nodes.line: Everyone I know paid the tithe, and none of us asked where it went. You don't even know your own name, and you're already asking. I'd sooner follow that than wait for the next wagon.

choices.text: Then walk beside me, not behind. I'll need someone who knows these hills.
Keep asking with me. Two people asking are harder to ignore.

nodes.speaker: $trusted
nodes.line: Beside, then. I know which holds will feed us and which will sell us. That's a start.

nodes.speaker: $trusted
nodes.line: Harder to ignore. And harder to tithe white, maybe.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Easy, I'm not with the Choir. I followed the smoke from Saltmoss. You're the ones who stole their white wagon?

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: That depends on who's asking, and why there's fire in your hand.

choices.text: We did. Want to help us keep it?
Who's asking?
Put the fire out first.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Help? I've wanted to set that wagon alight since I was old enough to spell "tithe". Keeping it is a new idea.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Someone from the fens. Someone the tithe line has missed twice, and I don't plan to give it a third go.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: That's not a threat, it's a habit. Fen folk keep a spark lit the way you'd keep a hand on a purse. There. Out.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: So what's a white wagon for, once it isn't the Choir's?

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: It was full of the tithe when we took it.

choices.text: Getting the tithe out of the Choir's hands.
It was the fastest thing in Saltmoss.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Good answer. Everyone on the moor gives that answer, right up until the Captain's riders crest the hill.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Ha. At least you don't dress it up. The last people who stole from the Choir called it a holy war.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Three of you against the whole moor, and the Captain on your heels. Why would anyone throw in with that?

nodes.speaker: $party:2
nodes.line: Show them the orb, Commander. Out here an orb is a dead stone, but near you they wake. We saw it at Saltmoss.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: That orb's been dead since before my grandmother was born. It's glowing. How is it glowing?

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The light steadies in the Commander's palm.

choices.text: It wakes near me. I don't know why yet.
Ride with us and find out.
Riding with us won't be safe.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Nobody on this moor admits to not knowing things. The Choir knows everything, and look where that got us.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: You're bargaining with my curiosity. It's working, and I'm annoyed that it's working.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: The tithe took my aunt. She walked out of the line white as chalk and never warmed again. If that orb can wake, maybe other things can too.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Safe is the tithe line. I watched my aunt walk out of one white as chalk. I'll take the moor.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Then I'm in. In the fens we know what the tithe really takes, and how to make it burn back.

choices.text: Glad to have you, Red Mage.
You can thank the one who spoke for you.
Keep that fire pointed at the Choir, not at us.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Glad to be had. Don't make me regret it before supper.

nodes.speaker: $party:2
nodes.line: Someone had to. You'd have talked yourself out of it otherwise.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Then I owe you a spark when you need one. Fen folk pay their debts. It's the Choir we don't pay.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Fair. I'll aim. I can't promise where it lands when the Captain's riders come.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: A white wagon with no white collectors on it. Now there's something you don't see.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: We're not Choir. Are you going to tell anyone?

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Not if you let me ride along. I've got lanterns, oil, and a very good map for twenty gold.

choices.text: Come with us.
We'll buy the map.
We don't need you.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Sold. And a potion for good faith. Now, about that ride?

choices.text: Come along.
We're fine.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Rude. I'm coming anyway. You'll need me.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Splendid. I'll set up shop in the back.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: That's a Choir wagon. And you're not Choir.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: You noticed. Are you going to turn us in?

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: The Choir asked me to forge their tithe chains. I said no. I'll fix your gear if you take me with you.

choices.text: Deal.
Prove you're any good.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Hand me your worst blade. There. Sharper than when you bought it.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Let's go before the Captain hears I'm missing.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: We've come a long way from Saltmoss. Those wrecks out there were people running, too. Can I ask you something?

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: Ask.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Why did you run with us? You'd only just woken. You owed us nothing.

choices.text: For the coin on that wagon.
For the people the tithe would have hollowed.
To find out why Halcyon's tech wakes for me.
For all of you.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Honest, at least. Coin buys bread, and the Choir had plenty. I won't judge.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: My village was tithed white. That's what I hoped you'd say. It's why I came.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Then we want the same answer. Whatever you are, the Choir wants to know it too.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: A family, then. A strange one, with a stolen wagon. But a family.

nodes.speaker: $commander
nodes.line: I don't remember much of who I was. I know who I'm running with. We keep going.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The knight from the Ember sits with their back to the fire, red-and-black armour still on, facing the dark where the Manalith hangs.

choices.text: You fought beside us a long while before you joined. Why now?
You've joined the caravan. Before we march, I want to talk.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: I was waiting to see whether you'd turn and kneel to the thing in the sky. You haven't yet. That's rarer than you think.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: You fight the Choir. So do we. That's enough of an oath for the Shardfall.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Where I come from we drink from the red rivers under the fallen shards. It burns going down. It's the Manalith's own body, and we take it into ours.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The knight's gauntlet tightens on a cup that isn't there.

choices.text: Then tell me what you want. I'd rather know than guess.
I don't know what the Manalith is. I'm not ready to decide its fate.
Whatever the Ember wants, here you follow my lead.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Most of us want it down. All the way down, broken open, done. I'm still deciding whether I'm most of us.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: An honest answer. The Shardfall's full of people who decided too early. Some of them are still burning.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Leaders. The Infernalists have those too. I'll walk behind you, Commander, but I'll keep my own eyes on the sky.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: You should know the Infernalists are Ember too. They'd open the Anchors wide to drag it here. Some of them were my friends.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: Far off over the Shardfall, a red glow pulses once and fades.

choices.text: Then we stop them, and we bring your friends home if we can.
You chose differently. That's what matters to me.
If they come for us, I'll need to know you won't hesitate.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Home. I haven't heard anyone say that word kindly in years. My blade's yours, Commander.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: I did choose. Some nights I'm not sure I chose right. Ask me again when we've seen the Shardfall together.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: I won't. That's the worst thing about the Ember, Commander. We never hesitate.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The newcomer from the Fen-dark has hung a bundle of drying reeds from the wagon's hoop and keeps glancing at the orb on the Commander's belt.

choices.text: You watched us from the reeds for a long time. I'm glad you came out.
You've joined the caravan. I'd like to know who's riding with us.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: In the fen you learn to wait and see what a stranger does with a wounded thing. You stopped for every one of them. So here I am.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: A healer goes where the hurt is, and the hurt is following your caravan. That's reason enough to ride with it.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: You should know I can see it. The colour in people. Yours is wrong, Commander. Too old, and too bright for how tired you look.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: Somewhere past the firelight, frogs start up all at once, then fall silent together.

choices.text: I was a commander of Halcyon. I died in the Still, and it brought me back.
I don't know what I am. I'd be grateful if you'd help me find out.
What you see in me is my business. Keep it to yourself.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Halcyon. We live in its ships, you know. Its Arks, lying in the mud where the tides threw them. Some nights the old doors still hum.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: An honest question. The Choir never asked one. Yes. I'll look, carefully, and tell you what I find, even if you won't like it.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: As you like. But the fen keeps secrets for a reason, Commander, and it's usually because the secret is dangerous.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Half the Fen-dark ran from the Choir's choirs. They taught the tithe songs once. They know what the Lullaby really takes, and they don't sing anymore.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The healer turns a small glass vial in their fingers. Something cyan glows inside it, faintly.

choices.text: Then help us understand it. We'll need everything you know.
Your people are safe with us. The Choir won't take them back.
Keep that vial away from the others until I know what it is.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Everything I know. That's a long night, Commander. Bring tea, and don't let it go cold.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Brave thing to promise. I'll hold you to it, gently, the way you hold a cut closed.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Fair. Careful is how the fen stays alive. It's only a little of someone's colour. I'm keeping it safe until they want it back.

payload.title: A new face at the fire

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The caravan's newest hero sits apart from the others, near the edge of the firelight, not quite sure of their place yet.

choices.text: You chose us after a long look. That counts for something.
You're one of us now. Come closer to the fire.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: I watched you long enough to know you weren't another collector with a kinder face. That's more than most get from me.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: One of you. I've been one of a lot of things. A caravan running from the Choir is new.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: The others say the old tech wakes when you're near. The orbs we fight with, the Halcyon doors. Is that true?

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The orb at the Commander's belt brightens a little, as if it heard the question.

choices.text: It's true. I don't know why yet. I'd like you to help me find out.
I came out of the Still. Halcyon's machines remember me, even if I don't.
It's true, and it's why you're safer with me than without me.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Help. Not follow. Nobody's asked me to help with anything that big before.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: The Still. They say nothing that goes in comes out. And here you are, by a fire, talking to me.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Maybe. Safe is what the Choir promises too, every time the collectors come.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: I paid the tithe like everyone. I know people who paid too much and came back Hollow. I want to know where it goes.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: Across the fire, someone laughs at a story, and the sound carries out over the dark.

choices.text: Then we find out together. That's the whole reason we ride.
Fight beside us and you'll see where it goes.
Some answers aren't worth the price. Be ready for that.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Together, then. I'll hold you to that, Commander.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Fighting I can do. Point me at it.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: I've paid prices before. At least this time I'll know what I'm buying.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The newcomer from the Free Holds has polished their gear twice since supper and is starting a third time.

choices.text: You took your time deciding. I'm glad you decided on us.
You've joined the caravan. Before you march with us, talk with me.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: In the holds you don't give your word to strangers. I watched how you treat the ones who follow you. That was what decided it.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: I took the place that was offered. Where I come from, that isn't nothing. A hold remembers who opened the gate.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: I swore an oath to my hold once. Then the Captain sold our tithe to the Choir and called it peace. So I ask you plainly: what do you want sworn?

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The fire pops. Somewhere behind the wagons a horse stamps in its sleep.

choices.text: Nothing. Stay because you choose to, every morning.
Swear to the people in the holds, not to me.
Swear to follow my orders. That's all I need.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: No oath at all. My grandfather would call that dangerous. I think it might be the most honest offer anyone's made me.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: The holds. The ones who paid and paid and got Hollow neighbours back for it. Yes. That I can swear to.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: The Captain wanted that too. I'll follow your orders, Commander, but I won't swear to them. Not again.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: You should know one thing. The Captain is still out there, hunting the runaways who took the Choir's caravan. Hunting you. Hunting me now.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The hold-knight's hand rests on their sword hilt, without gripping it.

choices.text: Then we face the Captain together, when the time comes.
The Captain broke the holds' word. We'll make it right.
Let the Captain hunt. We'll be gone before the dogs catch the scent.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Together. Good. I'd rather stand in that line beside someone than hear about it later from the road.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Make it right. You say it like you mean it. Then my shield goes where you go.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Running isn't the holds' way. But I've seen what the Captain brings, so I'll run with you, for now.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The traveller from the Lantern Road has hung a small paper lantern on the wagon's hook and lit it, though the camp has fires enough.

choices.text: You walked the road beside us for days before you joined.
You've joined us. Sit a while. I'd like to know who rides with me.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: The road teaches patience. I wanted to see where you walked when no one was watching. You walked toward people, not away from them.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: I came to the caravan because the road turned this way. On the Lantern Road that is reason enough.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: We keep the lanterns lit through the gorges, all the way to the pilgrim shrines. We do not ask why the Manalith hangs there. You ask a great deal, I think.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The little lantern's flame leans toward the Commander, though there is no wind.

choices.text: Somebody has to. The Choir counts on nobody asking.
I ask because I lost most of what I knew. I'm trying to find it again.
I ask the questions. You keep the light. That's how this works.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: The schools say a question is a blade without a guard. Still. I have carried this lantern for years and never once asked who it is lit for.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Lost. Then you are a pilgrim too, walking toward something you cannot see. The road is kind to those.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Simple roles. The sword-schools like them. I will keep the light, Commander. Mind that it does not show you only what you want to see.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: My master told me to walk the road and serve whoever needed the light. I did not expect it to lead to the Choir's tithe road.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The traveller sets one hand flat on the wagon boards, the way the monks greet a shrine.

choices.text: Then serve the ones on the road behind us. They need the light most.
Serve how you see fit. I won't tell you how to keep a lantern.
Keep up and keep quiet. The road ahead is not for pilgrims.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Behind us. Yes. That is the oldest teaching of the road, and you found it without being told. I will keep it lit.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: A Commander who leaves the lantern to its keeper. I will remember that when the road grows dark.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Quiet I can do. The road taught me that before it taught me anything else.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The new one from the Underspire sits on the wagon's tailboard, watching the camp the way a runner watches a street: every exit counted.

choices.text: You walked beside us a long way before you said yes.
You're with the caravan now. I wanted to hear it from you, not the roster.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: I wanted to see if you'd sell me out first. Everybody up top does, sooner or later. You had three chances and didn't take one.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: The roster's right. Food, a wagon, and somebody pointing the swords the same way. That's a better deal than the Underspire ever gave me.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Where I grew up, we lived under Halcyon's dead towers and stole light off its old taps. Then you show up and the dead tech starts humming. Who are you?

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The orb at the Commander's belt glows a little brighter, as it always does near Halcyon metal.

choices.text: I was a commander of Halcyon. I died in the Still, and it brought me back.
Someone the old machines remember. I don't remember much else.
Someone who pays you to fight. That's enough to know.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Died. In the Still. And walked out. Everyone in the Underspire has a story about that vault, and none of them end with somebody walking out.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Straight answer. I'll take a straight answer over a pretty one. Half the gangs down there lie about where they come from.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Fine. Bosses I understand. Redline had bosses. They all said that right before they asked for something worse.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: We dodged the Choir's collectors our whole lives. Ran the roofs when the white wagons came. Now I'm riding toward them on purpose.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The runner turns a stolen coin over and over between two fingers.

choices.text: Then teach the rest of us how to dodge them. We'll need it.
You don't have to run anymore. Not while you're with us.
Keep your eyes open. If this goes bad, I need to know first.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Ha. Nobody up top ever asked a Street kid to teach them anything. First lesson: never stand where the light's good.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Everybody runs, Commander. But I'll run in your direction for a while, and we'll see.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Eyes are the one thing the Street gave me for free. You'll hear it from me before anyone else does.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The newcomer from the Wild hasn't come near the fire. They sit in the long grass at the camp's edge, where a small red flower has opened between two stones.

choices.text: You followed the caravan for days. I hoped you'd come in.
You've joined us. Come sit where it's warm, and talk with me.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Animals follow a herd before they join it. You have to see if the herd eats its weak ones. Yours doesn't.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Warm is fine. Walls are not. If you want me close, don't put a roof over me.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Out in the Wild, things grow where the sky's pieces fell. Red things, in the white. The Choir says they're poison. They're not. They're just alive.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The red flower turns, very slightly, toward the orb on the Commander's belt.

choices.text: I'd like to see where they grow. Will you show me?

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: You'd come? Most people want to burn it. Yes. When the moon's right. You have to be quiet, though.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Good. Listening is the first thing the beasts teach you. Talking is the last, and most people never get there.

nodes.line: Safe. The white things in the Choir's halls are safe. Nothing grows on them at all. I'll stay close, but I won't stay tame.

nodes.line: Some of us have been touched by it. Changed a little. The Choir calls us Bloom-touched like it's a sickness. Does it scare you?

nodes.line: The wild child's eyes catch the firelight and hold it, a shade too red.

nodes.line: One of us. The beasts will like hearing that. I'll tell them tonight.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Scared and still sitting here. That's how a good tamer starts, Commander.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: I'll tell you. I tell everyone I trust when something new grows. You're on the list now.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Every shrine on this road has a board, and every board has names on it. Beasts, bandits, a deserter or two from the Red Seal.

nodes.line: That mural lit when I touched it. One moon, and nothing beside it. I know that sky. I don't know how I know it.

nodes.line: The sage on the stair says it's the oldest painting on the road, older than the Choir. Before the Manalith there was only the Moon. The pilgrims light lanterns to keep it asleep. I sell them the oil, and lately I wonder what I'm selling.

nodes.speaker: $trusted
nodes.line: As it comes. I'll be listening, Commander.

nodes.line: There's a ring burned into the shrine floor, and every lantern on the wall leans toward it.

nodes.line: A calling circle. Pilgrims used them to send for help along the road. Put coin in the bowl, and someone out there looking for a cause hears it.

nodes.line: Ours to tell you, yours to choose. The Innkeeper would keep it asleep, without the skim, and pay for it in people as gently as anyone can. nodes.line: Those cogs. Nobody cut those teeth. They grew.

nodes.line: The Bulwark march in white armour like they own Halcyon's streets. Six of them broken would make the Choir think twice about following us.

nodes.line: The Cathedral's ahead, and the Choir won't go easy on us. I don't think we're strong enough yet. Let's get there before we climb.

nodes.line: The ice maulers drink what leaks from the arches, and their cores never warm. Break three and bring me what's inside.

choices.text: We'll bring them.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: They'll still be out there.

nodes.line: Steel quenched in frost-core holds an edge forever. Two frost cores from the Wastes, and I'll show you.

choices.text: We'll get them.

nodes.line: Two cores. Keep them wrapped, or they'll freeze your hands.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith

choices.text: We'll dig some up.

nodes.line: The walkers out at the dig are plated with Halcyon steel. Three plates off the wrecks and I can make armour worth wearing.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith

choices.text: We'll do it.

nodes.line: The fen hags were Choir once. Now they sing mana into curses and bind them into their own claws. Three claws, and I might learn how they hold.

nodes.line: The Bloom grows trees where nothing should grow. Their heartwood burns warm for days. Three pieces would keep this camp alive through anything.

nodes.line: The Cathedral will hurt us more than anywhere yet. Learn to mend the whole party at once before we climb, and we'll all come back down.

choices.text: I promised we'd go to her first. That hasn't moved an inch, whatever else has.
You sent the warning on the next cart. Did anything ever come back?
I wouldn't turn the wagon for one hold. I was wrong. It was never one hold.
Wherever she is, she knows you're still standing.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: I know it hasn't. I've watched you keep every other promise on this road, and I've stopped counting the days till the holds. Nobody in a hall ever kept anything for me.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: One line, scratched on the back of my own letter. Not leaving. Hiding the spears in the well. Too stubborn to run and smart enough to make the levy short a few. That's her.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: No. It never was. You saying so now is worth more than the detour would have been. I mean that.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Still standing. Yes. That's what I'd want her to know, more than anything. That's what the shield's for.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: So. The second line. I've thought of a hundred words for it and none of them fit. You're the one I stand in front of now, Commander. You pick.

choices.text: Stand beside the ones who stand.
Stand before the road, and the road holds.
Leave it blank. You've earned not swearing anything to anyone.
Cut it later. Tonight, let me take the watch, the way you took it for us at the ford.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Beside. Not in front. Huh. A squire would never say that. I think I'm done being a squire. Hold the lamp, and I'll cut it now.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: The road holds. That's the hold's way of saying it, just longer. It'll fit on the rim. I'll cut it small and neat, the way my teacher did.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Blank. No. A knight without a line is just someone holding iron. I'll leave it for now, since you asked. But I'll fill it in someday, Commander, and it'll be about you whether you like it or not.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: You. Taking the watch. Nobody's ever stood in front of me. I don't think I know how to sleep behind somebody. I'll try. Wake me if anything comes over the ridge.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: Long after the fire is banked, a small red glow still moves at the edge of camp. The Red Mage sits on an upturned crate, turning a dented tin over and over, the lid cracked open on a single live coal.

choices.text: That glow carries. Choir scouts could see it from the ridge.
You can't sleep either?
Every night you sit with that tin. What's in it?

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: From the ridge? Through two hedges and a wagon? You think a great deal of Choir eyesight. Fine. I'll keep the lid lower. It isn't a lantern, anyway.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Fen folk sleep like herons, one eye at a time. And I don't like to sleep before this has settled. It sulks if I leave it too early.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: You've been counting. Good. I'd rather be watched by someone who notices things.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: It's a coal, Commander. The same one, more or less, for nine years. I feed it a pinch of peat and a breath of fire every night, and it keeps.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Red Mage tips the tin so the coal rolls, and blows on it once. It brightens like an eye opening.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: It came out of my aunt's hearth. The morning of her tithe she banked the fire like always, said she'd see to it when she was back. She came back. She never touched that hearth again. Sat by it, cold, every day, and never once asked for it to be lit.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: So I lifted a coal out before it died, and I've carried it since. Stupid, isn't it? A whole house went cold, and I saved one ember of it in a tobacco tin.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Red Mage snaps the lid half shut and waits.

choices.text: It isn't stupid. You kept what the tithe couldn't take.
What's it for, though? Nine years is a long time to carry a coal.
Grief that burns in a tin can burn down a camp. Be careful with it.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: That's a kinder way to say it than I've ever managed. I'll borrow it, if you don't mind. I'll tell it to the coal.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: I don't know yet. That's the honest answer, and you're the first to get it. I think I'm waiting to find out what it's for. That orb of yours made me think the wait might be nearly over.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: I've been careful for nine years, Commander. Careful is what kept it small. But I heard you. I'll keep it clear of the wagons.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Go on, get some sleep. I'll bank it and follow. One of us should be rested when the Captain comes over the hill.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The lid clicks shut. For a while the tin still glows faintly through the dent, then the Red Mage tucks it inside a coat and the dark settles back over the camp.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Red Mage has pulled a glove off to work a stubborn strap, and in the firelight the back of that hand is a map of old, shiny burn scars, laid one over another.

choices.text: Those burns are old. Not from any fight of ours.
Let the Cleric see to that hand.
Say nothing, and hold the strap steady for the Red Mage.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: No. Not from any fight with anyone. I did these myself, a little at a time, the winter after the tithe.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: There's nothing to see to. They healed years ago. They're only ugly, and I did them myself, the winter after the tithe.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Thank you. You didn't ask. Most people ask. I'll tell you anyway: I did these myself, the winter after the tithe.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: My aunt's hands were cold, Commander. Always. Hollow people's hands are. So every night I'd hold them and push heat into them, the way you'd warm a pot. A little more every night. Her hands never warmed. Mine burned instead.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: I stopped when she asked me to. Only thing she asked for that whole winter. Not because it hurt me. Because it didn't do anything, and she could see me hoping.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Red Mage's eyes go to the Commander's satchel, where the orb sits wrapped.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Here's what I keep coming back to. My fire never reached what the tithe took. But that orb wakes near you. Dead for a hundred years, and it wakes. What if fire near you could reach it too? What if it isn't heat a Hollow needs, but whatever you've got?

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Red Mage pulls the glove back on, carefully, and waits.

choices.text: When we next pass a Hollow who'll let us, we'll try. Together.
I don't know what I've got. I won't let you burn yourself again on a guess.
Maybe. But your aunt asked you to stop for your sake. Would she want you starting again?

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Together. I'm writing that down somewhere in my head where I can find it. If it doesn't work, it doesn't. But I'll have tried with someone, not alone in a cold kitchen.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: A guess is all I've ever had. You're telling me to keep my hands in my pockets and wait for someone else's answer. I've heard that before. From the Choir, mostly.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: No. She'd want me sleeping and eating and not looking at her like a sum to solve. I don't know how to stop wanting it, though. You might have to help me with that part.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: The coal's still in the tin, by the way. Nine years and a season. I haven't let it go out.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Red Mage pats the coat where the tin rides, and goes back to the strap. The knot comes loose on the first pull.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Red Mage sits by the cold fire pit with the dented tin open on one knee and a folded scrap of letter-paper on the other, read so often it has gone soft as cloth.

choices.text: You kept what the tithe couldn't take. I said it then. I'd say it again.
You told me you were waiting to find out what that coal was for. Did you?
I told you once to be careful with that tin. I was wrong to make it sound like a threat.
News from the fens?

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: I told the coal, you know. That very night. It didn't say anything back, but it burned a bit taller. Sit down. There's news.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: I think so. I think tonight's the night I find out. Sit down. There's news.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: You weren't wrong. You were a commander with a camp full of wagons. And I never once set one alight, did I? Sit down. There's news.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: From a cousin in Saltmoss who can barely spell, so it took a while to read. Sit down.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: My aunt sat by the cold hearth the way she always does. And then, out of nothing, she said my name. Asked where I'd gone. Nine years, Commander, and she never asked after anyone.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Red Mage turns the letter over, though the back is blank, and turns it again.

choices.text: We said we'd try together, with the orb. When the road goes back past Saltmoss, we will.
I wouldn't let you try. I think I was afraid of what it would cost you. I'm sorry.
You asked me to help you stop wanting to fix her. Maybe you don't have to stop. Maybe she's asking for you, not for a cure.
Then write back. Tell her where you've gone.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: You remembered. I wasn't sure you would. Then I'll stop counting the days and start counting the miles. That's a better kind of sum.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Afraid for me. Huh. Nobody's been afraid for me since I was small. I'm not sorry you said no. I'm glad you said that.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Asking for me. Not waiting to be mended. Just asking where I'd gone. I hadn't let myself read it that way. I think you're right.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: I will. I'll tell her I'm with a commander who stole the Choir's white wagon and talks to me like I'm worth answering. She'll think I've joined a circus.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: So. The coal. Nine years I've carried it, waiting for it to be for something. I think it's for tonight. I just don't know which way.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Red Mage holds the open tin out across the cold fire pit.

choices.text: Light the camp fire with it. Her hearth can warm all of us now.
Keep carrying it. Take it home to her hearth when we pass Saltmoss.
Let it go out. You've carried her long enough.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: All of you. Yes. She always did cook for half the lane. Stand back, Commander. It's been waiting nine years, and it's going to be pleased with itself.

nodes.line: Home. Back where it came out of, with me carrying it, and you beside me, and that orb of yours in your pocket. Whatever happens at that hearth, it won't be cold. I'll feed it twice as much peat till then.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Let it go out. Maybe. Maybe that's what she'd say too. Not tonight, though. Tonight I'll just close the lid and leave it to decide for itself. Goodnight, Commander.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The camp is asleep. At the back of the wagon, where the Sage sleeps nearest the satchel, a lantern is still lit, and the Sage is turning a length of knotted cord through both hands.

choices.text: Still mending, this late?
Put the lantern out. It can be seen from the ridge.
Couldn't sleep either. Mind the company?

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Not mending. Nothing to mend tonight, for once. I'm counting.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: It's Lantern Road oil. It burns low and it doesn't carry. Sit down, if you're up. I'm counting.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: The company's welcome. The counting isn't much to watch, but sit.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The cord is old and dark with handling. Every finger's width or so there is a knot, pulled tight, and there are a great many of them.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: One knot for every pilgrim who climbed the stair under the spire and didn't come down. I told you I counted them. I didn't say I counted them like this.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: On the Lantern Road, when somebody dies far from home, the healer who saw them last ties a knot and carries it back to their lantern. So the road knows. Nobody carries these back. So I carry them.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Here's what keeps me up, Commander. We're going up that stair. On the road, you tie the knot before the climb, not after, so nobody's forgotten if it goes wrong. Do I tie knots for us?

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Sage holds out the free end of the cord, the part with no knots in it yet.

choices.text: Tie one for each of us. If we don't come down, someone should know.
No knots for us. We're coming down, and you're coming with us.
Put the cord away. Counting the dead won't mend anyone.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Honest. Most people want me to say it'll be fine. I'll tie them loose, then. A loose knot can come undone on the way back down.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Coming down. You say it like you've already been up and back. I'll hold you to it. The end of this cord stays clean until you prove me wrong.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: It doesn't mend anyone. You're right about that much. But it isn't for mending. It's so somebody remembers they were here. I'll keep it, Commander. I'll just keep it where you don't have to look at it.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Go and sleep. Somebody bled today and somebody will bleed tomorrow, and I'd like the both of us awake for it.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Sage winds the cord round one wrist, three turns, and blows the lantern out.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Sage has the satchel open on a flat stone and every jar out of it in a row, and is sorting them again, though they were sorted at dusk.

choices.text: Something missing from the satchel?
You sorted those an hour ago.
Leave the jars. Tell me what's wrong.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: No. Everything's here. That's the trouble with a satchel. It's always got everything in it except the one thing.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: I did. Hands like to be busy when the head won't be. You'd know, if you ever sat still.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Straight to it. All right. Nothing's wrong tonight. Something was wrong a long time ago, and tonight it's loud.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Sage pulls the cord from a sleeve and holds up the first knot on it, the oldest, worn almost smooth.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: This one's Wick. My apprentice, off the Lantern Road. Wick came to the city with me to learn what the neon does with mana. Quick hands. Better at the salves than I ever was.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Then Wick's colour started going thin. You'll have seen it in the cities. The glow in the heartbeat fades a little more each week, and nothing in this satchel puts it back. I tried every jar. Twice.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: The Choir told Wick the Lullaby at the top of the spire would make it whole again. So Wick climbed. I tied the knot the morning after. I didn't tie it before. I was so sure I'd mend it first.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Sage turns the knot between finger and thumb and doesn't look up.

choices.text: If there's any trace of Wick at the top, we bring it down. I promise you that.
You couldn't mend what the Choir did. That was never yours to carry.
Wick chose the stair. Let Wick's choice be Wick's.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: A promise. From somebody climbing the same stair. That's either the bravest thing I've heard or the most foolish, and on the road those come out the same. I'll hold you to it.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Never mine. I've said that to a hundred people at a hundred bedsides. It's strange how little it helps when it's turned round. But it helps a little. Thank you.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Wick's choice. Yes, it was. Wick was grown, and stubborn, and wanted to be whole. I just thought I'd have the last word. Healers always think that. I'll climb with you anyway, Commander.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Sage puts the jars back one by one, the right way round this time, and buckles the satchel shut.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Nobody climbs alone. The road says it over every lantern. Wick did, though. I don't mean to let that happen twice.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Sage sits by the fire with the cord laid out straight along the ground, from the oldest knot to the free end, and is running a thumb along it, knot by knot.

choices.text: You tied us in loose, the way you said. Still loose?

I told you to put that away. I was wrong. Show me.
Counting again?

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Still loose. Every one of you. I check them every night, like a pulse. Sit down.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Still clean. I keep waiting to need it, and you keep not letting me. Sit down.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: You were half wrong. It doesn't mend anyone. But you asked to see it, and that's the half that counts. Sit down.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Not counting. Finishing. Sit down.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: I counted them again tonight. The same number as under the spire. Not one new knot since I've been walking behind this wagon. On the road, that's the longest I've ever gone.

nodes.speaker: character-commander
nodes.line: The Sage's thumb stops on the first knot, the one worn smooth.

choices.text: I promised we'd bring Wick down. That promise hasn't moved.
You told me it helped a little. Does it still?
I said Wick's choice was Wick's. I said it too easily.
Wick would know you never stopped counting.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: I know it hasn't. I've watched you keep every other promise on this road. I stopped bracing for the morning you'd take it back.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: More than a little, now. I mended a child in the last town whose colour was going thin, the same as Wick's. Not all the way. But I stopped blaming my hands while I did it, and my hands were steadier.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Too easily. Maybe. But you said it straight, and I was angry, and then I kept thinking about it. Wick did choose. I can grieve a choice without having to have stopped it. That took me a long while.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Never stopped. No. That's what the knot's for. So Wick isn't one more name the stair swallowed without anyone noticing.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: So. The clean end. On the road, when a healer's cord is done, they tie one last knot and hang it on their own lantern. I don't know what the last knot should be. You're the one I'm walking behind, Commander. You pick.

choices.text: Tie one for the first pilgrim who comes back down. It'll be us.
Hang it on the wagon's lantern. This is your road now.
Leave it undone. You've carried enough of the dead.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: The first one down. Nobody's ever tied that knot. I'll tie it now and leave it loose, and pull it tight the morning we walk off that stair.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: The wagon's lantern. There's no road oil in it, and it's never once gone out. Wick would have laughed at that. Yes. Hold the light still, and I'll hang it.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Undone. No. A cord with no end is just string. I'll leave it for now, since you asked. But I'll finish it someday, Commander, and the last knot will be yours whether you like it or not.

nodes.line: You saw the red in my blade. Most people run when they see it.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: We drink from the red rivers out here. It burns. Would you?

nodes.line: The Choir digs up the Manalith's shell and sells it back to us. What would you do about their dig?

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Let the fire settle. Then I'll know.

nodes.speaker: $hero

nodes.speaker: $with

payload.title: A walker of the Lantern Road

nodes.line: The lanterns burned brighter while you fought. The monks would call that a good sign.

nodes.speaker: $with

nodes.line: Out here you're the ones in the Choir's white wagon. So which is it: collectors or runners?

choices.text: Just travellers. The paint came with it.
Runners. We took the wagon so the tithe never got where it was going.
Collectors, in our own way.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Underspire rule one. What do you do when the Red Seal comes down your street?

choices.text: Split up, take the roofs, meet at the noodle stall later.
Stand there and pay. It's easier.
Hide and hope they pick another door.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: The whole Underspire runs its lights off Halcyon's old taps. Should we shut them off?

choices.text: Who cares? Lights are lights.
That's for someone smarter than me.
Not on our own. But we should know what they're pulling on.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Let me count what you said against what you did out there.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: You're all right. I'll run with your crew. Somebody has to watch your backs.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Nah. You talk like you've never been squeezed. Catch you around.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: The beasts here listen to me. They didn't mind you. That's rare.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: We didn't come to hurt anything that leaves us alone.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Out in the Bloom, red things grow where pieces of the Manalith fell. Should we burn them?

choices.text: Only the ones that bite.
No. Something growing isn't the same as something hurting.
Burn it all. It came from the sky.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: A wolf takes a sheep from a hold. Who's wrong?

choices.text: The wolf. Hunt down every one.
The wolf, I guess.
Nobody. The wolf is hungry and the hold is poor. Fix the hunger.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: If I come, my animals come too. Will your people mind fur in the stew?

choices.text: Bring them. A camp with beasts in it is never taken by surprise.
Leave them. They'll slow us down.
As long as they don't eat the rations.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Let me ask them what they think. They're thinking.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: They like you. So do I, a little. We'll come.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: They don't trust you. Neither do I. Off you go.
